# iOS App Store Publishing Plan

Minimum steps to get Boardsesh (`com.boardsesh.app`) from zero to published on the App Store.

This is the one-time, "from zero" setup. For per-release operational steps (signing, metadata upload, screenshots, submission), `app-stores/apple/app-store-submission-guide.md` is canonical — this plan points to it rather than re-documenting it.

**Current state:** Expo SDK 53 React Native app at `packages/mobile/`. The native iOS project is generated by `expo prebuild` from `packages/mobile/app.config.ts` (it is not committed). BLE permissions and usage strings are configured in `app.config.ts`. No Apple Developer account yet.

---

## Step 1: Apple Developer Account

1. Go to [developer.apple.com/programs](https://developer.apple.com/programs/) and click Enroll
2. Sign in with an Apple ID (or create one)
3. Choose enrollment type:
   - **Individual** ($99/year) — fastest, enroll as yourself. You can transfer to an org later.
   - **Organization** ($99/year) — requires a D-U-N-S number, takes longer (up to 2 weeks for verification)
   - **Recommendation:** Start as Individual to unblock everything. You can convert later.
4. Pay the $99 annual fee
5. Wait for enrollment approval — typically 24-48 hours for individuals

## Step 2: Certificates & Signing

Once your developer account is active:

Production builds go through **EAS Build** (`eas build --profile production -p ios`), which manages signing credentials (App ID, distribution certificate, provisioning profile) for you. The first EAS Build prompts to create or reuse these — let EAS manage them. No manual certificate creation needed for the shipping pipeline.

For a local build, generate the native project and sign through Xcode:

1. Run `vp run mobile:ios` to `expo prebuild` and produce the `packages/mobile/ios` Xcode project.
2. Open Xcode > Settings > Accounts > Add your Apple ID.
3. In the generated `packages/mobile/ios` project, select the **Boardsesh** target:
   - Set **Team** to your developer account
   - Confirm **Bundle Identifier** is `com.boardsesh.app`
   - Enable **Automatically manage signing**
4. Background Modes for BLE (if needed) are declared in `packages/mobile/app.config.ts` (`ios.infoPlist` / Expo BLE config) and flow into the project on the next prebuild — don't hand-edit the generated project, since prebuild overwrites it.

## Step 3: App Icons & Launch Screen

Both come from `packages/mobile/app.config.ts` and are baked into the native iOS asset catalog by `expo prebuild`. Don't hand-place anything in the generated `packages/mobile/ios` project.

**App Icon:**

- Source is `packages/mobile/assets/icon.png` (referenced by `app.config.ts` `icon`). A single 1024x1024 PNG with no alpha; prebuild generates the rest of the iOS sizes.
- Dev-variant icons regenerate via `vp run mobile:make-dev-icons`.

**Launch Screen:**

- Configured via the `expo-splash-screen` plugin in `app.config.ts` (`splash-icon.png`). Prebuild produces the native launch screen.
- Verify it looks good across device sizes by building a simulator app (Step 7).

## Step 4: App Store Connect Setup

1. Go to [appstoreconnect.apple.com](https://appstoreconnect.apple.com)
2. Click **My Apps** > **+** > **New App**
3. Fill in:
   - **Platform:** iOS
   - **Name:** Boardsesh
   - **Primary Language:** English
   - **Bundle ID:** Select `com.boardsesh.app` (created by Xcode in Step 2)
   - **SKU:** `boardsesh-ios` (internal reference, anything unique)
4. Fill in the **App Information** tab:
   - **Category:** Health & Fitness (primary), Sports (secondary)
   - **Content Rights:** Does not contain third-party content that requires rights
   - **Age Rating:** Fill out the questionnaire (all "None" — no objectionable content)

### Required Metadata

The live listing text (name, subtitle, description, keywords, URLs) is source-controlled in `fastlane/metadata/en-US/` and uploaded by the fastlane metadata lane — don't retype values here. For the canonical copy and the operational upload steps, see `app-stores/apple/app-store-metadata.md`.

**Support URL:** `https://boardsesh.com`

**Privacy Policy URL:** See Step 5

### Screenshots

Required sizes (minimum 1 per size class):

- **6.7" iPhone** (1290 x 2796) — iPhone 15 Pro Max / 16 Pro Max
- **6.5" iPhone** (1242 x 2688) — iPhone 11 Pro Max (if supporting older)
- **5.5" iPhone** (1242 x 2208) — only if you want to support iPhone 8 Plus class

Screenshots are generated by `vp run mobile:screenshots` (Maestro over iOS simulators, then fastlane deliver). Good frames to capture:

1. The board view showing an illuminated climb
2. The climb search/list view
3. The BLE connection screen
4. A queue / party session view

See `app-stores/apple/app-store-submission-guide.md` for the per-release screenshot and upload steps.

## Step 5: Privacy Policy & Legal

**Required before submission:**

1. Create a privacy policy page hosted at a public URL (e.g., `https://boardsesh.com/privacy`)
2. The policy must cover:
   - What data you collect (account info, usage data)
   - BLE usage (connects to climbing boards, no data transmitted off-device)
   - Third-party services (Aurora API, analytics if any)
   - Data retention and deletion
3. Add the URL to App Store Connect under **App Information > Privacy Policy URL**

### App Privacy (Nutrition Labels)

In App Store Connect under **App Privacy**, declare data collection. These are the canonical labels (source of truth: `app-stores/apple/app-store-metadata.md`):

| Data Type        | Collected?                        | Linked to User? | Used for Tracking? |
| ---------------- | --------------------------------- | --------------- | ------------------ |
| Email Address    | Yes (account)                     | Yes             | No                 |
| Name / Username  | Yes (account)                     | Yes             | No                 |
| Precise Location | Yes (party-session discovery)     | Yes             | No                 |
| Fitness Activity | Yes (climb ticks / logbook)       | Yes             | No                 |
| Usage Data       | Yes (Vercel Analytics, anonymous) | No              | No                 |

Nothing else is collected.

## Step 6: Review Info.plist

The Info.plist is generated by `expo prebuild` from `packages/mobile/app.config.ts` (`ios.infoPlist`). Edit the usage strings there, not in the generated `packages/mobile/ios` project. Verify:

- `NSBluetoothAlwaysUsageDescription` — explains that Boardsesh uses Bluetooth to connect to your climbing training board and illuminate routes.
- Location usage strings are present (precise location backs party-session discovery).
- No unnecessary permissions are declared (e.g. camera).

## Step 7: Build & Upload

The shipping build runs through **EAS Build** and EAS Submit / fastlane delivery — the `.github/workflows/ios-testflight-rn.yml` pipeline. To build and upload manually:

```
eas build --profile production -p ios
```

EAS handles signing (Step 2) and uploads the build to App Store Connect on completion. `eas.json` uses `appVersionSource: "remote"`, so version and build numbers are managed remotely — you don't bump them by hand.

For a local build (debugging the native shell, not for store delivery), use `vp run mobile:ios`, which runs `expo prebuild` plus a cached Xcode build of the generated `packages/mobile/ios` project.

The build appears in App Store Connect within ~15 minutes after processing.

## Step 8: TestFlight

1. In App Store Connect, go to your app > **TestFlight** tab
2. The uploaded build appears under **iOS Builds**
3. **Internal Testing** (up to 100 testers from your dev team):
   - Add testers by email under **Internal Group**
   - They get an invite immediately — no review needed
4. **External Testing** (up to 10,000 testers):
   - Create a group, add testers by email or share a public link
   - First build requires Beta App Review (~1-2 days)
   - Include test notes: "Requires a Kilter or Tension climbing board with Bluetooth for full functionality. Without a board, you can browse climbs and test the search/queue features."
5. Test on real devices — especially BLE connection with actual boards
6. Fix any issues, upload new builds (bump build number each time)

## Step 9: App Review Preparation

This is the highest-risk step. Apple may flag the app as a web wrapper (Guideline 4.2). Prepare carefully:

### Review Notes (visible only to reviewers)

Include this in the **App Review Information > Notes** field:

> Boardsesh requires a Bluetooth-enabled climbing training board (Kilter, Tension) for its primary functionality. The app uses native CoreBluetooth (via react-native-ble-plx) to:
>
> 1. Scan for and discover nearby climbing boards
> 2. Connect via BLE to the board's Nordic UART Service
> 3. Send LED illumination commands to light up specific holds on the wall
>
> This BLE functionality is not available in Safari on iOS, which is the primary reason for the native app.
>
> To test without a physical board: Open the app, browse climbs via the search screen, and tap any climb to view its hold layout. The Bluetooth connection screen (accessible from any climb detail) demonstrates the native BLE scanning UI.
>
> Video demo of BLE board connection: [include a short screen recording URL showing the app connecting to a real board and illuminating holds]

### Demo Video

Record a 30-60 second video showing:

1. Opening the app
2. Searching for a climb
3. Tapping "Connect" to start BLE scanning
4. Connecting to a real board
5. The board lighting up with the selected route

Upload to YouTube (unlisted) or similar, and paste the URL in review notes.

### Guideline 4.2 Mitigation

Apple flags minimal apps as too thin under 4.2. The app renders native React Native UI, not a website, so the "web wrapper" framing doesn't apply — but make the native value explicit:

- **Native BLE** (react-native-ble-plx / CoreBluetooth) is the core feature — impossible in Safari
- The app is **not functional without native Bluetooth** for its primary use case (board control)
- It is a native RN client end to end (climb browsing, search, queue, party sessions), not a wrapped web page

## Step 10: Submit for Review

1. In App Store Connect, go to your app > **App Store** tab
2. Select the build you tested via TestFlight
3. Fill in **What's New** (for first version, this is your initial description)
4. Set **Release Options:**
   - **Manually release** — recommended for first submission so you control the launch timing
5. Click **Submit for Review**
6. Review typically takes 24-48 hours (can be up to a week)
7. If rejected:
   - Read the rejection reason carefully
   - Respond in Resolution Center with clarifications
   - Fix issues and resubmit
   - Common first-time rejections: metadata issues, missing privacy policy, guideline 4.2

## Step 11: Release

1. Once approved, the status changes to **Pending Developer Release** (if you chose manual)
2. Click **Release This Version**
3. The app goes live on the App Store within 24 hours (usually faster)

---

## Timeline Estimate

| Step                            | Duration            | Blocker?                             |
| ------------------------------- | ------------------- | ------------------------------------ |
| Developer Account enrollment    | 1-2 days            | Yes — blocks everything              |
| EAS-managed signing setup       | 30 minutes          | No                                   |
| App icons & screenshots         | 1-2 hours           | No                                   |
| App Store Connect setup         | 1 hour              | No                                   |
| Privacy policy                  | 1-2 hours           | Blocks submission                    |
| Build & upload (EAS Build)      | 30 minutes          | No                                   |
| TestFlight testing              | 3-7 days            | Good practice, not strictly required |
| App Review submission           | 1-3 days for review | Yes                                  |
| **Total (fast path)**           | **~1 week**         |                                      |
| **Total (with proper testing)** | **~2 weeks**        |                                      |

## Checklist

- [ ] Enroll in Apple Developer Program ($99/year)
- [ ] Let EAS Build manage production signing credentials (local: sign generated project in Xcode)
- [ ] Confirm app icon in `app.config.ts` (1024x1024, no alpha)
- [ ] Verify launch screen via a simulator build
- [ ] Create app record in App Store Connect
- [ ] Confirm listing copy in `fastlane/metadata/en-US/` (see `app-stores/apple/app-store-metadata.md`)
- [ ] Take required screenshots (`vp run mobile:screenshots`)
- [ ] Create and host privacy policy at boardsesh.com/privacy
- [ ] Fill out App Privacy nutrition labels (Email, Name, Precise Location, Fitness Activity = Linked; Usage Data = Not Linked)
- [ ] Verify Info.plist usage strings in `app.config.ts` (`ios.infoPlist`)
- [ ] Build and upload via EAS Build production profile (local: `vp run mobile:ios`)
- [ ] Test via TestFlight on real devices
- [ ] Record BLE demo video for reviewers
- [ ] Write App Review notes explaining native BLE functionality
- [ ] Submit for App Store Review
- [ ] Respond to any review feedback
- [ ] Release the app
